# AndesCycle: RISC-V CPU Simulator

AndesCycle is a high-performance, Verilator-based simulator for Andes RISC-V CPU cores. It provides **cycle-accurate simulation with pipeline visualization**, debugging capabilities, waveform analysis, and support for advanced features such as ACERVV.

## Step 1: Get the simulator

### Option 1: Download released binaries for Linux x86-64

https://gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/vsim/releases

This is the easiest way to get started, but you cannot use ACERVV or dump waveforms.

### Option 2: Build from Dockerfile
Modify `config.yaml` to keep only the CPU you want and remove the others to reduce build time. Then run:

```bash
./build-docker.sh dev
```
Launch the container. You can then modify the code and rebuild to use ACERVV.
```bash
docker run -it --rm localhost/andescycle-dev:v0.15
```

### Option 3: Build from source
Make use of `.devcontainer`, or launch the container manually to build vsim inside, so
that you don't need to worry about some required third-parties like verilator.

```bash
docker build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
docker run -it --rm -v$PWD:/work localhost/vsim-env:latest
```

Modify `config.yaml` to keep only the CPU you want and remove the others to reduce build time. Then run
this inside the container.

```bash
./build.sh
```

## Step 2: Compile your demo code

Please refer to another repository: [vsim-demo](https://gitea.andestech.com/ycc738/vsim-demo).

To measure the exact cycle count of a code segment, read the `mcycle` CSR like this:
```c
csrr a1, mcycle
```

## Step 3: Run it

```bash
./sim_ax46mpv_advanced yourELF
```

To view the pipeline, run:
```bash
./sim_ax46mpv_advanced yourELF --kanata output.log --objdump yourELF.dump
```

Then open the `output.log` using Konata, see next step.

To learn more, use `--help` to see available usage.

## Step 4: Download Konata to view the pipeline
**[Konata Pipeline Viewer](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata)**

## 📖 Documentation

### User Guides
- **[Pipeline Analysis](docs/PIPELINE.md)** - Visualizing CPU performance with Konata
- **[ACERVV Support](docs/ACEDPI.md)** - Andes Custom Extensions RVV


### Developer Resources
- **[Development Guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)** - Contributing and coding standards
- **[CPU Configuration](docs/CPUCONFIG.md)** - Adding new CPU variants


### Debugging with GDB
```bash
# Compile with debug symbols
riscv64-elf-gcc hello.c -O2 -mvh -g -o hello

# Start simulator (runs JTAG server on port 9104)
./sim_ax45mp_plain hello --jdtm-rbb-port 9104

# In another terminal, connect GDB
riscv64-elf-gdb hello
(gdb) target remote :9104
(gdb) load
(gdb) continue
```

## 📊 Performance Benchmarks

| CPU | Simulation Speed | Platform |
|-----|------------------|----------|
| AMD Ryzen 9 5950X | ~9 KHz | Zen 4 |
| Intel i7-12700K | ~7 KHz | Alder Lake |
| AMD Ryzen 7 3700X | ~5 KHz | Zen 2 |

# andesim_abi

The shared wire-format contract for the Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator. These
headers define the bytes exchanged across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. They are
consumed by three independent components, so they live in their own repo and
are pinned as a submodule by each consumer (one source of truth, no drift):

| Consumer | Repo | Mounts this as |
|----------|------|----------------|
| `andesim` (QEMU TCG plugin + C++ driver) | top repo | `include/` |
| `hybrid_vsim` (vsim / SystemC + Verilator) | submodule | `external/andesim_abi/` |

Both mount points put this repo's root on the include path, so every consumer
includes the same way:

```c
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
```

## Layout

```
hybrid/
  state_abi.h        struct hybrid_state_v1 -- the wire format
  state_abi_check.h  compile-time offset/size lock (static_assert)
  insn_match.h       handoff marker HINT recogniser
  handoff_site.h     translate-time trigger capture + post-trigger PC
  v_drain_policy.h   pure V-state drain gate decision
  reg_names.h        GDB register-name tables (gdbstub wire contract)
tests/
  abi_compile_check.{c,cpp}  include every header from C and C++
  check.sh                   compile both as C11 + C++20
```

## Contract rules

- Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host). Not
  endian-portable.
- Never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add fields by consuming
  bytes from `reserved`, or bump to v2. `state_abi_check.h` locks every offset;
  a layout change must update it in lock-step and bump `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`.
- Both C and C++ must keep compiling these headers.

## Test

```sh
tests/check.sh        # host gcc/g++, zero external deps
```

A pass means the headers are self-contained from the repo root and the
`hybrid_state_v1` layout matches the locked offsets.

## History

Started fresh at the submodule split; the pre-split history of these headers
lives in the `andesim` repo under `include/hybrid/`.
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build this repo's vsim inside the Dockerfile's env-stage container image.
#
# What it does (README Option 3):
#   1. Build the `env` target image (verilator + toolchain) from ./Dockerfile.
#   2. Run ./build.sh inside that container with the repo bind-mounted at /work,
#      so build artifacts land in ./build/ on the host.
#
# Trim config.yaml to the CPU(s) you need first to cut build time.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Container runtime: prefer podman, fall back to docker.
if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=podman
elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=docker
else
  echo "error: need podman or docker on PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "error: missing $ROOT/Dockerfile" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# build.sh / cmake pull in external/ submodules; bail early if they are empty.
if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/external/fmt/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
  echo "error: submodules not initialized - run:" >&2
  echo "  git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT"

"$RUNTIME" build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
"$RUNTIME" run --rm \
  -v "$ROOT:/work" \
  -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest ./build.sh

## 0.5 Quick start with `./andesim`

`./andesim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
self-builds on first use). It drives `run` itself, orchestrating QEMU and
vsim directly; building is done by `scripts/build_all.sh` (which delegates to
`setup.sh`, `scripts/build_*.sh`). Sections 1-7 document those underlying
scripts (`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) for when you need to bypass
the driver.

Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:

```sh
bash scripts/build_all.sh                             # qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
./andesim list engines                                # discover the built engines
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one marker-mode handoff
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                          # the hybrid e2e suite (or scripts/test_all.sh for unit+contract+e2e)
```

Expected last line of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`:

```
summary: marker <N>p/0f/<S>s  pc <N>p/0f/<S>s  neg <N>p/0f/0s  total <N> passed, 0 failed, <S> skipped
```

Subcommand cheat sheet:

| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `./andesim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
| `bash scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]`               | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `plugin`, `fixtures`, `runtime` (qemu and vsim are external prebuilt binaries, not built here). |
| `./andesim doctor`                                             | Read-only environment health check: artifacts, submodules, toolchain, runtime, discovered engines, and `/dev/shm` mmap tiers (with WSL2 advice). |
| `./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] [--gdb [--gdb-port PORT]] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff and REQUIRES `--trigger marker|pc` to delimit the ROI; --gdb pauses at startup for a debugger: fast opens QEMU's GDB stub on port 1234, cycle halts the hart and opens vsim's JTAG port (9104) then execs `$ICEMAN`, a GDB server (use a modern OpenOCD); --gdb not supported with hybrid). |
| `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (env: `FILTER`, `MODE`, `JOBS`)        | Run the hybrid e2e suite directly (qemu+vsim round-trips). |
| `bash scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit\|contract\|e2e]`     | Run the full test surface: C++ unit tests + driver contracts + the e2e suite. |

Run `./andesim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
`ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal developer-only flags and the `list fixtures`
target). The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andesim`
(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).

---

### 2.5 Requesting memory (`--mem-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)

By default every `./andesim` invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:

| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| `--mem-size SPEC` | flag on `run` (`--mmap-size` is the old alias) | request guest program memory (`SPEC` = `128M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes). Cap `2G` minus one 4 KiB V-transport page (the AE350 DRAM window). |
| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | pin the backing directory (skips the tier list below). |

Per-model semantics of `--mem-size`:

| Model    | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| `hybrid` | `--mem-size` is your **program** RAM (default `128M`). The driver maps one extra 4 KiB page on top for the V-register transport scratch (L26): the physical shared mmap = QEMU memory backend = vsim RAM window = `--mem-size + 4 KiB`, with the scratch parked in that top page, just above everything your program can address. You get your full `--mem-size`; the page is invisible. The driver rejects `> 2G - 4 KiB` **before** allocating, and rejects an ELF whose static image would extend into the reserved page (`raise --mem-size`). |
| `fast`   | forwards a plain QEMU `-m`. Without the flag the argv is untouched -- QEMU as-is, its own 128 MiB default, no mmap involved. No `2G` cap here (that ceiling is the hybrid shared-mmap window, not fast's); QEMU itself validates the size and rejects only oversized values (`Cannot model more than 16GB RAM` on the AE350 machine). |
| `cycle`  | validate-only: the cycle engine always models its full DRAM window, so there is nothing to size (the driver says so on stderr). |

Backing-directory selection (`./andesim`): a two-tier list, first fit
wins (fit = size + 256 MiB free):

1. `/dev/shm` -- tmpfs, RAM speed. Skipped when absent or too small.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) -- disk-backed; the
   size ceiling becomes disk free space. Hot pages still sit in the
   kernel page cache, so the cost vs tmpfs is background writeback only.

We never switch **silently**: the status line always names the chosen
dir, and a fallback adds the reason, e.g.
`[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))`.
`HSIM_MMAP_DIR` pins a single dir with **no** fallback past it: rc=2
with a hint if it can't hold the request.

Examples:

```sh
# Small request; /dev/shm fits, so tier 1 is chosen.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 256M
#   [hsim mmap] 256.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 252.0 GiB)

# Near-max request on a small-RAM box: falls through to the disk tier,
# and the status line says so. (2047M is the hybrid ceiling -- exactly 2G is
# rejected because the extra V-scratch page would overflow the DRAM window.)
./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
#   [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))

# Pin a scratch filesystem instead (no fallback past the pin):
HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch \
  ./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
```

If you pin `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/tmp` and `/tmp` is mounted as tmpfs (Arch
default), that does not lift the RAM ceiling; pick a directory on a
non-tmpfs filesystem (`/var/tmp`, `/scratch`, etc.) -- or just let the
tier list pick `~/.cache/andesim` for you.

The hardcoded `mktemp -p /dev/shm` paths in the shell harnesses
(`tests/e2e.sh`, `tests/drivers/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) all use
128 MiB and are unaffected.

### 2.5.1 Running on WSL2 and macOS

The hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU and vsim) on **one Linux
kernel**, with the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel.
That rule decides what each OS needs:

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap dirs on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or just let the
  tier list fall through to `~/.cache/andesim`.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see the `mmap tiers:` section and the
WSL warnings at the end of its report).

**macOS** -- run-only. vsim is a Linux binary, so `./andesim` re-execs
the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in the podman machine VM;
the mmap lives inside that VM (the container's `/dev/shm`), never on a
virtiofs mount. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096   # the VM hosts /dev/shm (tier 1)
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>         # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work; builds (`scripts/build_all.sh`) stay Linux-only. The image is built on
Linux from `Dockerfile.runtime` (it bakes a fully built repo at
`/opt/hybrid_sim`); Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation,
so expect slower wall-clock than a Linux host.

### 2.6 The hybrid guest memory map (`--print-memmap`)

Which addresses may a hybrid workload touch? Print the map for exactly the
run you are about to do (same `--engine` / `--mem-size`; the ELF is optional
and only adds a fit note):

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

Reading the table:

- **END is the inclusive last byte**; SIZE is the region span.
- **DRAM** tracks `--mem-size`; the **V-scratch** page above it belongs to
  the V-register transport (2.5) -- the driver rejects an ELF that reaches
  into it.
- **ILM/DLM/HVM** rows appear only when the engine can actually transport
  their content (`--describe` sizes > 0, the backdoor gate); their bases come
  from the engine's own `--print-qemu-config` geometry -- the same file the
  QEMU leg boots with -- so the printed map IS the run's effective one.
- **Devices**: only the vplat set both engines model is listed. Device STATE
  never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART/SimControl
  instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT in the table is unsupported in hybrid mode: it is modeled by
  one engine only (QEMU's PLIC/PLMT/MROM/virtio..., vsim's debug-module
  window), so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

The map is hybrid-only surface: `--mode fast|cycle` run one engine's native
map, which the driver does not model (`--print-memmap` errors there). vsim's
own `--print-memmap` dumps its interconnect routing table -- useful for
engine bring-up, but it is one engine's view, not the hybrid contract;
`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh` cross-checks the two so they
cannot drift apart.

| `--mem-size SPEC` | flag on `run` (`--mmap-size` is the old alias) | request guest program memory (`SPEC` = `128M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes). Cap `2G` minus one 4 KiB V-transport page (the AE350 DRAM window). |

Per-model semantics of `--mem-size`:

| Model    | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| `hybrid` | `--mem-size` is your **program** RAM (default `128M`). | `fast`   | forwards a plain QEMU `-m`. Without the flag the argv is untouched -- QEMU as-is, its own 128 MiB default, no mmap involved. wins (fit = size + 256 MiB free):

1. `/dev/shm` -- tmpfs, RAM speed. Skipped when absent or too small.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) -- disk-backed; the

#   [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))

### 2.5.1 Running on WSL2 and macOS

The hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU and vsim) on **one Linux
kernel**, with the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel.
That rule decides what each OS needs:

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap dirs on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or just let the
  tier list fall through to `~/.cache/andesim`.

### 2.6 The hybrid guest memory map (`--print-memmap`)

Which addresses may a hybrid workload touch? Print the map for exactly the
run you are about to do (same `--engine` / `--mem-size`; the ELF is optional
and only adds a fit note):

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

Reading the table:

- **END is the inclusive last byte**; SIZE is the region span.
- **DRAM** tracks `--mem-size`; the **V-scratch** page above it belongs to
  the V-register transport (2.5) -- the driver rejects an ELF that reaches
  into it.
- **ILM/DLM/HVM** rows appear only when the engine can actually transport
  their content (`--describe` sizes > 0, the backdoor gate); their bases come
  from the engine's own `--print-qemu-config` geometry -- the same file the
  QEMU leg boots with -- so the printed map IS the run's effective one.
- **Devices**: only the vplat set both engines model is listed. Device STATE
  never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART/SimControl
  instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT in the table is unsupported in hybrid mode: it is modeled by
  one engine only (QEMU's PLIC/PLMT/MROM/virtio..., vsim's debug-module
  window), so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

The map is hybrid-only surface: `--mode fast|cycle` run one engine's native
map, which the driver does not model (`--print-memmap` errors there). vsim's
own `--print-memmap` dumps its interconnect routing table -- useful for
engine bring-up, but it is one engine's view, not the hybrid contract;
`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh` cross-checks the two so they
cannot drift apart.

## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use

| Mode     | Profiles          | Switch boundary                                          | Cycle figure           |
|----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| marker   | a kernel          | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1` insn match (markers in source)         | kernel cycles          |

--mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc`. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle`
delta.

Decision flow:

```
Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?
  binary is yours to edit          -> marker (andesim_ROI_begin()/end() around it)
  not editable, symbol/PC at ends  -> PC   (./andesim run --mode hybrid
                                            --trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E)
```

**Hardware-config sync.** A hybrid run models ONE core on two engines, so
the QEMU fast leg inherits the selected engine's hardware config. Three
things flow from engine to QEMU, all derived from the engine's frozen
`config.inc`:

- **VLEN** comes from the engine's `--describe` (512 when the engine
  reports none) and shows in the run banner as `vlen=N`.
- **The ISA** (extensions: CoDense, Zfh, Zba/Zbb/Zbc/Zbs, `xandesv5isa`,
  ...) comes from the engine's `--print-qemu-config`: the driver captures
  that QEMU `-readconfig` cfg and hands it to the fast leg, so QEMU executes
  the same extensions the engine models instead of a fixed `-cpu` string.
  An engine built without the flag (an older binary) makes the driver fall
  back to its default `-cpu` with no error. See `docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md`.
- **ILM/DLM content** (`--describe` `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`, bytes): when the
  engine has local memories, the fast leg's plugin also drains their content
  into `<state>.ilm`/`.dlm` sidecar files and the vsim leg loads them back
  (`--ilm`/`--dlm`), so a program that stages code/data in TCM before the ROI
  resumes with that content in place. An engine without local memories (or an
  older binary that does not report them) adds nothing. A guest that uses TCM
  must enable it itself (write `milmb`/`mdlmb`) -- which real TCM firmware
  does anyway; that CSR write rides the v6 write-mask so the enable is
  restored on the vsim leg. See `ROADMAP_ilm_dlm.md`.
- **HVM content** (`--describe` `hvm_size`, bytes): same contract for the
  High-Bandwidth Vector Memory at `0x90000000` -- the plugin drains
  `<state>.hvm`, the vsim leg backdoor-loads it (`--hvm`), and the exit
  drain dumps it back next to the handoff-out state. A program that stages
  vector data in HVM before the ROI resumes with that data in place; there
  is no enable bit (the geometry CSRs `mhvm_cfg`/`mhvmb` are read-only
  constants both sides derive from the same config). See `ROADMAP_hvm.md`.

An engine whose XLEN is not 64 (e.g. `vsim:d23`, rv32) cannot share
architectural state with the rv64 fast leg and is rejected with a clear
error.

**Preview the commands (`--dry-run`).** Add `--dry-run` to **any** mode
(`fast`, `cycle`, or `hybrid`) to print the exact engine command line(s) --

# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed

# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:<cfg>]
# sim_<cfg> prog.elf --resume-from-qemu <tmp>/state-0.bin --handoff-out ...

Supported VLEN range: 128 to 1024 bits. The handoff state file reserves
128 bytes per vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX`); an engine whose
VLEN exceeds 1024 is refused with a clear error instead of silently
truncating the V registers. A standalone fast run defaults to the
vector-capable CPU `andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32), so RVV
binaries run out of the box at the cpu model's built-in VLEN; andesim itself
passes no `vlen`. To pin an exact VLEN, add a `-cpu` through the passthrough
tail, e.g. `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256`
(the last `-cpu` wins).

Where `--` args land depends on the mode. `fast`/`cycle` forward them to their
single engine (qemu / vsim). `hybrid` has **two** legs (a QEMU fast-forward and
a vsim measure leg) whose command lines the driver builds itself, so there is no
single "the engine" to forward to -- `hybrid` therefore **rejects** `-- args`

the dedicated flags (`--kanata`/`--objdump`); to pin VLEN, pick the right

**`cycle` output.** A `cycle` run prints just two things: the program's own
output, then the cycle count as andesim's own one-line result --

```

instruction at `--pc-start` executes

> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a

### 4.3 Capturing a Kanata pipeline trace of the ROI

When debugging a hot path on vsim, pass `--kanata FILE` to `./andesim run`
in marker or pc mode. The resulting trace contains pipeline records only
for the ROI region (between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain) -- vsim
boot and DMI resume overhead are filtered out.

```sh
# marker mode: the ROI is the span between the two ROI markers (slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1)
# markers already in the source. vsim auto-derives the window.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata

# pc mode: the ROI bounds are whatever PCs you passed.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
```

Add `--objdump FILE` so the kanata `L` records embed the disassembly
text next to each PC. Generate the dump once with the toolchain
`objdump -d`:

```sh
$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf > /tmp/roi.S
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata --objdump /tmp/roi.S
```

Open `/tmp/roi.kanata` in [Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata)
to view the pipeline.

Constraints:

- `--kanata` is only valid with `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` or `--mode hybrid --trigger pc` (the only triggers with a single ROI-exit PC); any other trigger is rejected with rc=2.
- marker mode requires exactly one `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit marker) in the
  ELF. If the binary has more than one, vsim errors out with
  `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use \`--mode hybrid --trigger pc\` with explicit \`--pc-end\``.
  Switch to pc mode and pick the desired exit explicitly.
- `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

How it works:

- `./andesim` appends `--kanata FILE --kanata-roi`
  (and `--objdump FILE`) to vsim's argv.
- vsim's `--kanata-roi` flag defers the kanata enable until after
  `--resume-from-qemu` loads the input state and `enable_hybrid_handoff`
  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
    `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` PC from CsrTrigger (marker mode)
  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
    close on first retire of end_pc).

### 4.4 Verifying a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

With the QEMU2 handback removed, the code after your ROI never runs, so a
hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(default OFF) cross-checks the run's correctness:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify your_prog.elf
# ...
# [marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
# [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
# [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
